description: baseline

Replace the template recipe in submissions/arena/ with an airbench96-style port. Architecture: a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening first conv, with whitening computed in prepare from training patches; Dirac init; 3 residual groups of 3 convs at widths 128/384/576; BatchNorm-GELU. Optimizer: Nesterov SGD, lr 9.0 (airbench scaling), wd 0.012, batch size 1024, triangular LR schedule, 9 epochs, label smoothing 0.3. Data: the dataset stays on the GPU in fp16/channels_last; random crop (pad 2) runs on the GPU; derandomized alternating flip. No TTA and no torch.compile yet. Eval is a plain forward pass with no state changes. Build warms up eager kernels and cuDNN on synthetic tensors for train batch 1024 and eval B in {1, 1024}. This is the base recipe every other idea builds on.

On the E-port recipe, change only the epoch count: 9 → 8.5 if the port clears 0.753 with at least 0.3 pp margin, otherwise 9 → 10. Everything else stays identical, so this measures the local accuracy-vs-time slope that sets how far epochs can be cut.

On the port, compile the model's forward+backward with torch.compile (mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs') in build. Compile and warm up on synthetic inputs for the train batch shape and the ragged last-batch shape, and in eval mode for B in {1, 7, 512, 1024} (mark the batch dimension dynamic for eval, or fall back to the eager model for eval). Also replace the per-param SGD loop with a foreach/fused SGD. Math stays unchanged.
I003 re-run: compile+fused SGD with channels_last warmup (stride-guard fix)

On the port at 9 epochs, add Lookahead/EMA of weights in the airbench96_faster style: update every 5 steps, alpha ramping as in the reference, final weights set to the EMA copy. All EMA state is created and reset in prepare. The forward pass is unchanged.

Explore. On the port backbone, switch the conv filters to Muon: Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized Nesterov momentum, lr about 0.24, momentum 0.6. Keep SGD for BatchNorm params, whitening bias and the head. Batch size 2000 with the same epoch count. Newton-Schulz runs in bf16 with a foreach-style batched implementation.

Explore. On the port, apply progressive resizing: the first about 40% of epochs at 24 px, the next 30% at 28 px, the rest at 32 px (random-resized-crop on the GPU via F.interpolate). Warm up every resolution in build on synthetic data. Epoch count unchanged.

Exploit. On the E007 recipe (Muon + Lookahead/EMA + progressive resizing 24→28→32 px, 9 epochs), change only the epoch count from 9 to 8.5. Keep the resolution split as fractions of total steps (about 40/30/30%) and stretch the LR and EMA schedules to the new step count. Warm up every resolution in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path. Set torch._dynamo.config.error_on_recompile=True after build so a leak fails loudly. This spends part of E007's 0.60 pp margin and measures the slope with EMA and Muon on.

Exploit. On the E007 recipe at 9 epochs, change only the end of the LR schedule: decay linearly to exactly 0 instead of 0.07 of peak, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups (BN, whitening bias, head). The warm-up, peak and Lookahead/EMA schedule stay unchanged. This tests whether EMA and a lower final LR are only partly redundant, which the E005 post-mortem predicts.

Exploit. On the E007 recipe, narrow only the last residual group from 576 to 512 channels (the airbench96_faster width). Keep everything else the same, including the Muon lr, epochs and resizing schedule. Re-warm-up all compiled shapes in build.

Exploit, building on E007's finding that time scales with pixel count. On the E007 recipe at 9 epochs, use a more aggressive resolution schedule: the first 30% of steps at 20 px, then 30% at 24 px, 20% at 28 px, and the last 20% at 32 px. Each resolution is compiled and warmed up in build with channels_last synthetic batches of the exact training shape. Use error_on_recompile after build. Keep the global max-pool head so the network works at every size.

Diagnostic that sharpens I013 for the current tip; it makes no recipe change. Run the E010 recipe exactly as committed (Muon, Lookahead/EMA, 24→28→32 px, 9 epochs, last group 512) offline on held-out seeds 3-12 through the same harness code path. Record per-seed accuracy, the 10-seed mean, the std and the offset from the seeds 0-2 mean (0.7548). In the same pass, record per-epoch CUDA-event times to settle H3.3.1. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

Exploit, as a near-free accuracy lever (W1 and W3 crux). On the E010 recipe, change only the label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 (the airbench96_faster value) in the training loss. Epochs, resizing, Muon/SGD settings and Lookahead/EMA stay the same, and so do the compiled shapes. Since the loss changes only by a constant, no extra warm-up is needed beyond the usual error_on_recompile check.

Exploit. On the E010 recipe, change only the Muon learning rate for the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.36 (×1.5). The SGD groups (BN, whitening bias, head), momentum 0.6, batch size 2000, schedule shape, epochs and Lookahead/EMA stay the same. The 0.24 value comes from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon, and E006's surprise gain (+0.66 pp, outside every member's range) suggests the CIFAR-100 optimum has not been explored.

Explore. On the E007 recipe, capture the train step (forward, backward, Muon Newton-Schulz plus SGD update, and the EMA update on steps where it applies) in CUDA graphs. Use torch.compile mode='max-autotune' (cudagraphs on) or a manual torch.cuda.graph per resolution with static input buffers that the GPU augmentation writes into. Capture every resolution in build on synthetic data. Math stays identical.

Exploit, as the second point of the coarse grid. On the E010 recipe, halve only the weight decay for all parameter groups (Muon conv filters and SGD groups), keeping the same decoupled or coupled form the code uses now. Everything else stays identical. Short runs with EMA may need less regularization than the 0.012 CIFAR-10 value.

Explore, settling the W2/W4 crux about launch versus compute. Run torch._dynamo.explain and a short torch.profiler trace offline on the E010 train step on synthetic data: GPU augmentation, forward/backward, Muon+SGD step, Lookahead/EMA update and LR schedule. If there are graph breaks or host syncs (for example .item(), Python-scalar LR, or tensor-to-bool checks), remove them: keep LR as a GPU tensor, fold augmentation into the compiled region, and keep the math identical. Commit only the break-free version and record the measured GPU idle fraction in the notebook.

Exploit. Tests a proposed new child of H2.3: accuracy is set mainly in the final 32 px phase, so the 28 px middle phase can be dropped cheaply. On the E015 recipe (Muon, Lookahead/EMA, CUDA graphs, 9 epochs, last group 512), change only the resolution schedule from 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps to 24/32 px at 70/30% of steps. The 32 px tail keeps exactly its current step count and position, so the LR and EMA schedules stay the same. Build no longer needs the 28 px graph; keep the 24 and 32 px warm-up and capture, and keep error_on_recompile on after build.

Diagnostic, making no recipe change. It replaces I025, which pointed at E015, and answers the main crux of W1, W2, W3 and W5: is E016's 0.7607 real margin or a reshuffle? (1) Run the committed E016 recipe offline on held-out seeds 3-12 through the harness code path (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Record per-seed accuracy, the 10-seed mean, the std and the offset from 0.7607. (2) Secondary, for H4.3.1: clear the inductor cache and rebuild E016 in a fresh process, run seeds 0-2 again, and record whether the per-seed accuracies are bit-identical and how far the 3-seed mean shifts. (3) While doing this, read the true optimizer step count from the code for H4.2.3. E012's per-epoch timing listed 10 epoch loops, the last about half length, which suggests about 9.5 true epochs. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

Exploit: spend the margin on the epoch dial. On the current tip, cut 1.0 true epoch uniformly. That is E016, about 9.5 → 8.5 true epochs (verify the step count in code first; H4.2.3). If the 24/32 swap idea was kept first, cut only 0.5 true epoch from it instead. Resolution phases stay fixed fractions of the total steps (so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share), and the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008. Compiled shapes are unchanged, and error_on_recompile stays on.

Explore/exploit on the biggest FLOP block. This replaces I028, rebased on E016. Group 2 (128→384 at 15×15, then two 384→384 convs at 7×7) is about 51% of conv MACs, and its width also feeds group 3's first conv. On the E016 recipe, narrow only group 2 from 384 to 320 channels (a multiple of 64, so tensor-core tiles stay aligned). Group 1 (128), group 3 (512), Muon lr and wd, epochs, the resizing schedule and Lookahead/EMA stay unchanged. Recapture every resolution's graph in build, with error_on_recompile on.

Exploit, as a time-neutral accuracy booster that would fund the trims. E016's post-mortem points to the BN-bias wd (bias lr = 64 × lr) as the active part. On the E016 recipe, cut weight decay to ×0.25 of the original on the SGD groups only (BN biases, whitening bias, head), leaving the Muon conv-filter wd at E016's ×0.5. First check in code whether the filters are renormalized; if they are, filter wd is inert and this is equivalent to a global cut. Nothing else changes. Recapture the graphs if wd is baked in as a constant.

Exploit: test the untested −0.5 point of the epoch dial. Apply it to the current tip: E017, or I033's recipe if I033 is kept. Cut 0.5 true epoch uniformly, for example about 9.5 → 9.0 true epochs; read the exact step count from the code first (H4.2.3). Resolution phases stay fixed fractions of total steps (40/30/30, so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share). The LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008/E020. Compiled shapes are unchanged and error_on_recompile stays on. Changing the step count also changes RNG consumption, so seeds 0–2 get re-rolled. So in the same session, run the recipe offline on held-out seeds 3–12 (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Base keep or discard on both numbers, not on the 3-seed mean alone. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase a lucky seeds-0–2 draw.

Explore W5's crux (proposed H2.3 child): the accuracy cost of the low-res phases depends on the final feature-map regime (3×3 vs 2×2 after group 3), not on pixel count. Feature-map sizes: 32→31/15/7/3, 28→27/13/6/3, 26→25/12/6/3, 24→23/11/5/2. E018 replaced the 28 px phase (3×3 regime) with 24 px (2×2 regime) and lost 0.68 pp. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the middle phase from 28 px to 26 px, keeping the 40/30/30% step split. The 26 px phase stays in the 3×3 regime with about 14% fewer pixels. Warm up and capture the 26 px graph in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, and keep error_on_recompile on. Judge accuracy on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as on seeds 0–2.

Exploit, as a time-neutral accuracy booster to fund trims (W1 crux: does a stronger or longer EMA add 0.3 pp?). E005 showed end-of-run averaging is worth about 1 pp on CIFAR-100, and E009 showed a lower final LR adds nothing on top of it, so averaging strength is the untuned part. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the Lookahead alpha ramp exponent from 3 to 2: alpha = 0.95**5 * (step/total)**2 instead of **3. The averaging then pulls harder from about mid-run on. Update frequency (every 5 steps), the final full copy, LR schedule, epochs and resolution all stay unchanged. Alpha is a per-step tensor or constant, so recapture the graphs if it is baked in. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. This proposes a new H1.3 child: the airbench96 averaging schedule is under-tuned for CIFAR-100 short runs.

Explore. This is the single-factor version of E011, separating its two confounded changes. On the E016 recipe, change only the first phase: the first 15% of steps run at 20 px, followed by 24 px for 25%, 28 px for 30% and 32 px for 30%. The 32 px tail keeps its exact step count and position, and the LR and EMA schedules are unchanged. Warm up and capture the 20 px graph in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, with error_on_recompile on.

Exploit: spend the margin on the epoch dial, with a branch that depends on I038, which is still running. Base: the current tip E023 (9.0 true epochs), or I038's recipe if I038 is kept. Branch (a): if I038 is kept with a held-out seeds 3–12 gain of at least 0.15 pp, cut 0.5 true epoch to 8.5 true epochs (212 steps at batch 2000). This is E020's step count plus I038's averaging. Branch (b): otherwise, cut 0.25 true epoch to 8.75 true epochs (219 steps). In both branches the resolution phases stay fixed fractions of total steps (40/30/30, so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share), and the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008/E020/E023. Compiled shapes are unchanged and error_on_recompile stays on. The step count changes RNG use, so in the same session also run held-out seeds 3–12 (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Keep only if seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 and the held-out mean is at least 0.7535. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase a lucky seeds 0–2 draw.

Explore/exploit: a FreezeOut-style backward truncation, a mechanism not yet tried in this loop. On the E023 tip, put group-1 conv filters (Muon) and the whitening bias plus group-1 BN params (SGD) in their own param groups. Their LR schedule follows the global triangle up to its peak, then decays linearly to 0 at 75% of total steps. The other groups keep their schedules. For the last 25% of steps, all of them at 32 px, detach group 1's output before group 2, and use a second compiled train step that does no group-1 or whitening backward and leaves group-1 params out of the Muon/SGD update. Group-1 BN still runs in train mode, and Lookahead still averages every param. Capture both 32 px step variants (full and truncated) in build with channels_last synthetic tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Back-of-envelope: group 1 is about 20% of conv MACs at the largest maps, so skipping its weight-grad and input-grad work saves about 14–18% of a 32 px step (including memory-bound BN/GELU backward), applied to about 2.0 s of tail time. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

Exploit, a time-neutral accuracy booster. The tip's population mean is now below the bar (held-out 0.7526), so the next time cut needs one first. On the E027 tip (8.75 true epochs, 219 steps at batch 2000, 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%), change only the LR warm-up length. First read the current warm-up and peak fraction from the code (airbench96 uses a peak at about 0.23 of steps). Halve it so the peak comes earlier, with the same peak value and a linear decay to the same 0.07 floor, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups. The Lookahead/EMA ramp, resolution phases, epochs, wd and LS all stay unchanged. If LR is a GPU tensor, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture every resolution in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if the held-out gain is at least 0.15 pp and seeds 0–2 clear 0.753.

Exploit, a time-neutral averaging booster in the direction opposite to E025 (which pulled harder and hurt by 0.27 pp held-out). D003 (C0024/C0025) points to the reset interval as the untuned Lookahead knob. On the E027 tip, change only the Lookahead update interval from every 5 to every 10 steps. Rescale the per-update retention so the total pull per step is unchanged (alpha_10 = alpha_5**2 at each ramp point, same exponent 3), and keep the final full copy. LR, epochs, resolution, wd and LS stay unchanged. Recapture the step graphs if the interval or alpha is baked in, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

Explore: proposes a new H2.4 child. Drop easy examples using free per-sample losses from the main net, with no proxy. The committee vetoed I041 for the proxy's cost; this version adds no extra forward passes. On the E023 tip, change the compiled train step to return the per-sample loss (reduction='none', then mean for backward) and scatter it into a GPU loss buffer indexed by sample id. The buffer is created and reset in prepare. From epoch 2 onward, each epoch's shuffled order uses only the 90% of samples with the highest loss in the previous pass (torch.topk on the GPU, then the usual GPU shuffle). The batch stays at 2000 and the ragged remainder is dropped. Total steps fall from 225 to about 205 (1 + 8×0.9 epoch-equivalents). The resolution phases (40/30/30), LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules are fractions of the new total step count. Alternating flip still uses each sample's own pass parity. Warm up the modified step in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

Exploit, a time-neutral booster that targets the end-point, where averaging forms (E005 showed the late phase is worth about 1 pp). On the E027 tip, keep label smoothing at 0.3 for the first 85% of steps and set it to 0 for the final 15%, which lies entirely inside the 32 px phase. Pass LS as a GPU scalar into the compiled loss, or capture a second 32 px step variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Nothing else changes. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

Exploit and crux test (W1/W5: is early low resolution close to free?). Run it on the E027 tip, or on the tip plus any booster above that was kept with at least +0.15 pp held-out. Change only the resolution split from 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30% of steps to 30/10/30/30%. The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact step counts and positions, and the LR and Lookahead schedules are unchanged. The 20 px graph is already captured in build, and error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 and the held-out mean stays at or above 0.752 (the 40-seed official bar of 0.75 then has at least 0.2 pp of headroom).

Exploit: stack the free lever (the freeze) with the cheapest accuracy booster (epochs). Start from the E027 tip and apply E028's freeze exactly as committed in fcacfc6. Group-1 conv filters, the whitening bias and group-1 BN params get their own param groups. Their LR follows the global triangle to its peak, then decays linearly to 0 at 75% of total steps. For the last 25% of steps, use the truncated compiled 32 px step: group-1 output detached, and no group-1 or whitening backward or update. Group-1 BN stays in train mode and Lookahead averages every param. Then change only the step count: 8.75 to 9.25 true epochs (about 231 steps at batch 2000). Read the exact count from the code. The resolution phases (20/24/28/32 at 15/25/30/30%), the freeze point (75%), and the LR and Lookahead schedules stay fixed fractions of the new total. Capture full and truncated 32 px variants in build with channels_last synthetic tensors, with error_on_recompile on. In the same session, run held-out seeds 3–12. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase seeds 0–2.

Exploit and crux test (W5: does a math-identical change keep the tip's per-seed outcomes?). Base: the current tip (E027, or the H2.6.2 successor if kept). Change only systems work in prepare, keeping every number bit-identical. (1) Move the training images to the GPU as uint8 and do the float conversion, normalization and channels_last/fp16 cast on the GPU, in the same op order and dtype the CPU path uses now. (2) In build, run prepare's GPU kernels once on synthetic uint8 tensors of the real shape: the whitening patch extraction and eigendecomposition, the normalization and the allocations. This removes trial 0's 0.21 s first-call cost. The whitening is still computed from the same images as now; do not subsample. Before launching, check offline with torch.equal that the normalized train tensor and the whitening weights equal the current ones. If they don't, adjust the op order until they do, or abandon. Record per-trial prepare time.

Exploit. First read the code. If the whitening bias already stops training before 25% of steps, close H2.6.3 without a run. Otherwise, on the H2.6.2 successor (or E027 if it is not kept), stop the whitening bias's gradient after 20% of steps (Hiverge; airbench96 trains it for 3/45 epochs). Use a third compiled step variant in which the whitening output is detached, so no input-grad of group 1's first conv and no whitening backward on the 31×31 maps. Group 1 still trains normally until the freeze. Anneal the whitening-bias LR to 0 by 20% of steps. Capture the new variant at every resolution it runs at (20/24/28/32 px) in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

Exploit, the freeze dose. Run only once the H2.6.2 successor is kept, and on it. Move the group-1 and whitening-bias freeze start from 75% to 60% of steps. The group-1 LR is annealed to 0 by 60%. Everything else is unchanged, including the step count, resolution phases and LR/Lookahead schedules. The truncated step now also runs during the last 10% of the 28 px phase (60–70%), so capture a truncated 28 px variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep if held-out ≥ 0.7545 and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753, or if the held-out loss is ≤ 0.1 pp and a follow-up epoch top-up is planned.

Validation diagnostic, with no recipe change. Run it immediately after a candidate tip is kept (the H2.6.2 successor, or whatever is the tip once H2.6.3/H3.2.1 are stacked). Seeds 3–12 have driven about 10 keep decisions and carry a winner's curse. Run the committed recipe offline on fresh seeds 13–22 through the harness (benchmark.run --seed 13 --n 10). Record per-seed accuracy, mean and std, and the pooled 20-seed mean with its SE. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

Explore, the next memory-bound lever on the frozen stem. On the H2.6.2 successor (or the freeze recipe in fcacfc6), at the freeze point: run one no-grad train-mode forward of group 1 over the current batch to set its BN running stats. Use the existing buffers if their values are already the frozen-phase stats. Then, for the frozen phase, put group-1 BN in eval mode and fold scale and shift into the conv weights and biases (done inside timed train, once). The truncated step then runs group 1 as conv+bias+GELU under no_grad, with no BN statistics reductions on the 31×31 maps. Lookahead still averages the unfolded params. Keep the unfolded copies so the final weights and BN buffers stay consistent: either fold only in the compiled frozen forward, or unfold before the final copy. Eval uses the standard model. Capture the new truncated variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

Exploit: finish the early-resolution dial. The tip is E036 (9.25 true epochs, about 231 steps at batch 2000; 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%; whitening bias detached after 20%; group-1 freeze at 75%). Change only the resolution split, from 30/10/30/30 to 40/0/30/30: the 24 px phase (about 23 steps) now runs at 20 px. The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact step counts and positions. The LR, Lookahead, whitening-detach and freeze schedules stay unchanged. The 20 px graphs (full and whitening-detached variants) are already captured in build. The 24 px graphs can be dropped from build. error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2, and discount held-out by about 0.1 pp for the winner's curse (E038). Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545.

Exploit: non-uniform trim. Run it on the I-40/0/30/30 successor if kept, otherwise on the E036 tip. Remove only 12 steps from the 20 px phase (231 → 219 total steps). The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts. The whitening-bias detach stays at the same absolute step (about 46). The group-1 freeze still covers the same last ~58 steps. The LR triangle and the Lookahead ramp are stretched to the new total as fractions, as in E023/E027. No new shapes, so no recapture is needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Run held-out seeds 3–12 in the same session. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545.

Explore/exploit: staggered FreezeOut, which separates where E037's cliff came from. First read group 1's structure in the code. If, as in airbench, the pool follows group 1's first conv, that conv (24→128 on 31×31 maps) and the pool are the only full-resolution work left once the whitening is detached. On the E036 tip, put only group 1's first conv in its own Muon param group. Its LR follows the global triangle to its peak, then is annealed to 0 by 60% of steps. From 60% on, detach that conv's output (before the pool), so there is no conv1 wgrad and no pool/BN backward on the 31×31 maps. The rest of group 1 keeps E036's annealed freeze at 75%. Capture the conv1-detached variants at 28 px and 32 px in build, with error_on_recompile on. Lookahead still averages every param. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. If the code shows the pool is not right after conv1, freeze whichever layers run at 31×31 instead, and record which ones.

Explore diagnostic, with no recipe change. It sets the value of the remaining stem levers (H2.6.4/H2.6.5/H2.6.3) and the PCIe-transfer caveat in H4.3. Offline, run torch.profiler on the tip's compiled 32 px full step and truncated step, and on the 24 px step, with batch 2000 and synthetic channels_last data. Record GPU time by kernel class (conv GEMM fwd/dgrad/wgrad, BN, GELU, pool, elementwise, Muon NS, Lookahead) and by layer group (whitening, group 1, 2, 3, head). Also record achieved conv TFLOP/s per group. Write the table to the notebook and label each kept lever as compute-bound or bandwidth-bound. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

Exploit: a booster that leaves the training trajectory unchanged. It replaces I064 with a paired design that has no trajectory noise. On the E036 tip, at the end of train() and after the final Lookahead copy (which lerps BN running_mean/var from different fast weights and never recomputes them): reset every BN layer's running stats, set momentum=None (cumulative average), run a no-grad train-mode forward at 32 px over K batches of 2000 training images with the usual crop and flip, then restore momentum. Capture this forward-only graph in build on synthetic channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Eval stays a plain forward pass. Judge it with an offline instrumented copy on unselected seeds 13–32. In each trial, evaluate the averaged model once before recalibration and once after, so the two numbers share the exact same trained weights and the difference has no trajectory or rebuild noise. Do the same for K=1 and K=3. Commit the better K, then run ar.py to get time and the seeds 0–2 check. The submission evaluates only once.

Explore/booster, the step-count crux (W3, W5). E041 found that removing early 20 px steps cost as much as a uniform trim. That suggests early accuracy is carried by optimizer steps, not by pixels. On the E036 tip, use batch 1000 instead of 2000 only during the 20 px phase (the first 30% of data passes, so about 69 steps become about 138). Same data and same pixels; only the step count and per-step overhead change. Key the LR triangle, the whitening-bias detach (20%) and the resolution switch to data progress (samples seen), so they land at the same data point. In this phase, scale the SGD-group lr linearly (×0.5) and keep the Muon lr per step unchanged. Lookahead stays every 5 steps; alpha is near 0 this early. From 24 px on, batch 2000 is unchanged, so the 24/28/32 phases, freeze and Lookahead tail are identical. Capture batch-1000 graphs at 20 px, both the full and whitening-detached variants, in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds (reuse E038's 13–22 and run E036 once on 23–32; the C/D/selection ideas share this baseline), plus seeds 0–2.

Exploit, staggered FreezeOut cascade. This is the only remaining backward-truncation lever that targets the largest block, group 2 (~51% of conv MACs). On the E036 tip, put the group-2 conv filters (Muon) and group-2 BN params (SGD) in their own param groups. Their LR follows the global schedule until 75%, then decays linearly to 0 by 90% of steps; E028's annealed freeze is what kept group 1 neutral. For the last 10% of steps (about 23 steps, 32 px, group 1 already frozen), detach group 2's output before group 3 and use a new compiled 32 px step with no group-1/2 backward and no update for those params. Group-2 BN stays in train mode, and Lookahead still averages every param. Capture the new variant in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds, plus seeds 0–2.

Explore diagnostic, with no recipe change. It replaces I058 and adds the overhead accounting from W5's crux. Explore/exploit: remove the last full-resolution tensor from the stem. Keep the same channel counts, BN-GELU after it, init scheme and RNG draw order (same weight shape). The whitening detach (20%) and group-1 freeze (75%) stay unchanged. Keep I082 as queued: the group-2 freeze dose test. Base: the E049 tip (237 steps; group-2 LR annealed 75%→0 at 90%; last 10% group-2-frozen). Explore, proposing a new H2.6 child: the stem needs a steady adaptation signal, not a gradient on every step. Intermittent stem backward in the 28 px phase, which is the most expensive phase (about 71 steps × ~26 ms ≈ 1.8 s). On the E049 tip, on every second step of the 28 px phase (40–70% of steps), use the group-1-detached 28 px step variant. That variant has no group-1 wgrad/dgrad and no BN/GELU backward on the stem maps, and group-1 params get no Muon/SGD update and no momentum-buffer change on those steps. The variant already existed in E037's commit 6293350. On the other steps, run the usual whitening-detached full step with the group-1 LR as scheduled. Do not rescale the LR: single factor. Group 1 still trains on every step at 20/24 px and from 70% to 75% at 32 px, so it still adapts through the 28→32 switch, which E037/E042 say it needs. Lookahead averages every param. Capture the variant in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E049 baseline, plus seeds 0–2.

Exploit: a time-neutral test that separates the two parts of the freeze-dose cost. On the E061 tip (225 steps), change only the end point of the group-1 LR anneal (conv filters on Muon; BN params on SGD): it moves from 75% to 80% of steps, so group 1's LR decays more slowly over the whole run. The group-1 detach stays at 75% (same absolute step), so the frozen variant covers exactly the same steps and time is unchanged. At the detach, the group-1 LR is then about 5/57 ≈ 9% of peak instead of 0. E009 and C0021 say the LR floor does not matter under Lookahead averaging. Whitening detach, group-2 freeze, resolution, step count, Lookahead and LS are unchanged. If the LR is a GPU tensor table, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 (60 draws) against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. This is the time-neutral form of H2.6.13.
